To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) PMs may be less informed than is socially optimal; (2) campaign contribution limits increase social welfare by reducing this problem; (3) PMs may have an incentive to acquire information strategically; and (4) PMs may choose to remain on the fence to maximize their bargaining power.
(i) a politician has a preference for being less informed than may be socially desirable, and (ii) contribution limits can improve policymaker incentives for information acquisition.

(i) a PM's optimal policy-making strategy is to remain under informed about policy issues and (ii) contribution limits increase the probability that the PM is on the fence, thereby decreasing the intensity of the lobbying competition.
